audit.whatIsWrong: Early text framed the lane as an even cooldown-bait war without the numbers that decide it.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 4 seconds of cover on a 25/23/21/19/17s cooldown against Ahri's 12-second Charm and 7-second Q. The trade of cooldowns is heavily in Ahri's favour as long as no projectile is thrown into the wall.
audit.corrected: Bait the wall, then own the next 20 seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] claimed 'his auto-attack resets off Wind Wall'.
audit.why: Wind Wall has no auto-reset and no attack interaction at all — it blocks projectiles for 4 seconds. The real crit spike is Steel Tempest, which the kit text states is treated as a basic attack and scales with the same things, on a flat 4-second cooldown.
audit.corrected: Crit items make Steel Tempest itself the damage, not the wall.
sources: brief enemyKit Q and W text

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent: Last Breath requires an airborne target, and Sweeping Blade cannot be recast on the same enemy for a few seconds.
audit.why: Kit text: 'Blinks to an Airborne enemy champion' — with no Steel Tempest knockup ready, his 70/50/30s ultimate does not exist. And 'Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds' means his dash chain needs fresh units, so his exit is readable and chargeable.
audit.corrected: Break his Steel Tempest stacks by stepping out, and charm him on the dash that has no next target.
sources: brief enemyKit R and E text

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Wall carries a derived 'terrain — creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' flag.
audit.why: Riot's own description is 'Creates a moving wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds' — projectiles only. Per the trust-the-description rule I made no claim that the wall stops Spirit Rush's dash; Spirit Rush's bolts are flagged projectile on Ahri's side, so the bolts are what it eats.
audit.corrected: The wall eats the bolts, not the dash.
sources: brief enemyKit W text vs derived flags

audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer, and whys[5] (his crit spike) and whys[6] (your items catch up) describe exactly the content shape.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side Skill, phases[5].side Yasuo, phases[6].side Ahri, with ratings realigned.

edits.before: Still a mechanical back-and-forth with no clear kit advantage for either side yet.
edits.after: Still mechanical: he cannot re-dash the same minion, so his escape path is readable.

edits.before: Yasuo's Wind Wall completely denies your Orb of Deception's return damage and his Sweeping Blade dashes let him reposition around your Charm, making trades an even mechanical back-and-forth.
edits.after: Wind Wall eats your orb for 4 seconds on a 25-second cooldown and Sweeping Blade repositions him around Charm — but he cannot re-dash the same target, so his exit is readable if you count units.

edits.before: Your Spirit Rush gives you a burst window his Last Breath knock-up can't easily punish if you engage on your terms, letting you win the all-in right as ultimates come online.
edits.after: Last Breath only blinks to an airborne target, so without a Steel Tempest knockup ready his 70-second ultimate does not exist — engage on your terms and Spirit Rush wins the all-in outright.

edits.before: Once he has Infinity Edge/crit items his auto-attack resets off Wind Wall and dash procs start shredding your health bar faster than your combo can answer.
edits.after: Once Infinity Edge and crit are online, Steel Tempest counts as a basic attack and crits with them, so his 4-second Q plus dash procs shred you faster than your combo answers.

edits.before: Level 1 favors him slightly since he can Wind Wall your early poke attempts and his passive shield soaks trades while he waits for a dash opening. From levels 2-4 it evens out into a mechanical skirmish — whoever baits the other's cooldown (Wind Wall vs Charm) first usually wins the exchange. Play patient, don't waste Orb into a wall, and look for moments when his dash is down.
edits.after: Level 1 he can wall your poke and his passive shield soaks the trade while he waits for a dash opening. From 2-4 it evens into a bait war, and the maths favours you: Wind Wall is 25 seconds at rank 1 against your 12-second Charm and 7-second Q. Never throw a projectile into a live wall, and step up when there is no minion left for him to dash onto.

edits.before: Right at 6 you get a real edge: Spirit Rush lets you burst him down fast if you engage on your own terms, since his Last Breath knock-up doesn't stop your combo the way it stops squishier mages without mobility. Push this window hard, because it's temporary — once his crit items come online the damage race swings back his way.
edits.after: Right at 6 you get a real edge: Last Breath needs an airborne target, so with no Steel Tempest knockup ready your combo goes unanswered. Spirit Rush's bolts are projectiles and the wall eats them, but the dash itself still travels — go past the wall first, then commit. Push this window hard; once crit lands the damage race swings back.

edits.before: Once Yasuo has Infinity Edge and crit chance rolling his damage output spikes hard, but once your own build catches up your burst combo comes back online fast enough to answer him, and your mobility lets you dictate when fights happen rather than dueling into his strongest window — respect the gap right after his spike, then take back control once itemized.
edits.after: Once Infinity Edge and crit are rolling his damage spikes hard, but your build catches up and your burst answers again — and his ultimate still needs a knockup to exist at all. Respect the window right after his spike, then dictate the fights: flank, charm him with no unit to dash to, and never duel inside a wall you watched go up.

edits.before: Punish his dash cooldowns after he uses Sweeping Blade to reposition
edits.after: Punish him when no minion is left to Sweeping Blade onto

edits.before: Yasuo wins by landing Wind Wall, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Yasuo wins by walling your combo, stacking Steel Tempest to a knockup, and turning that one airborne moment into Last Breath.

edits.before: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget R Spirit Rush (last dash) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Yasuo Wind Wall: matchup-defining — 4 seconds up, 25 seconds down at rank 1. Hold every projectile until it is spent, then step in. - Steel Tempest is a 4s cooldown and counts as a basic attack; its second stack is the knockup that makes Last Breath exist.

edits.before: Carry through picks — a landed charm is a won fight, and your dashes manufacture charm angles no one wards against.
edits.after: Carry through picks — charm him with no minion left to dash to, and a Yasuo with no knockup has no ultimate and no exit.

edits.before: If Yasuo gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Wind Wall extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q clears and stay relevant through charm picks.
edits.after: If Yasuo gets a kill his crit scaling arrives early — stop trading through the wall, farm with Q from 970 range, and commit only when Steel Tempest has no stacks and no unit sits between you.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt the map: shove with Q, dash-flank every river, and charm-pick Yasuo's teammates until the lane lead is a game lead.
edits.after: Ahead, starve the crit: shove with Q so he misses waves, then dash-flank elsewhere — a Yasuo without items is a melee with a 25-second wall.

edits.before: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Throw a half-range Q and watch: four seconds of wall, then twenty-plus seconds where every projectile you own lands clean.

edits.before: Q through his last-hit so both hits land, W if he eats the return, and walk — repeat until the charm window is lethal instead of optimistic.
edits.after: Sweeping Blade cannot re-target the same enemy for a few seconds, so charm him on the dash that has no follow-up target and he is stranded.

edits.before: Yasuo burns Wind Wall on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Minions are his dash road — hold the wave where you want the fight.

edits.before: That is Yasuo’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Extended means his passive shield rebuilds and Steel Tempest reaches its knockup.

edits.before: The last dash is your life insurance — an Ahri who spends all three going in is an assassin's favorite story.
edits.after: His passive shield eats the opener, and a spent charm is 12 seconds with no answer to the knockup that follows.

edits.before: Charming on cooldown for chip damage and then facing his real engage with nothing — the charm is the matchup, not the poke.
edits.after: Standing still is how Steel Tempest reaches its knockup stack, and that knockup is the only door Last Breath ever has.

edits.before: Track Yasuo’s Wind Wall: Blocks every projectile for its duration — hold your poke until it is spent. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Wind Wall (4s up, 25s down at rank 1): every projectile you own dies in it, Spirit Rush's bolts included. Bait it first.
